transcript:
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Korva Coleman.
Stocks opened mixed this morning as oil prices inched lower.
NPR's Scott Horsley reports the Dow Jones industrial average slipped about 75 points
in early trading.
Oil prices have backed off their recent peaks, but remain elevated as a result of the U.S.
war with Iran.
AAA says retail gasoline prices dip 2 cents a gallon overnight to an average of $4.46
a gallon; diesel prices are averaging just under $6.44 a gallon; higher jet fuel prices
are driving up the cost of airline tickets, just as many people are booking flights for
upcoming holiday travel.
The cost of airline tickets in August was up more than 23 percent from a year ago.
Australia's central bank raised its benchmark interest rate today for the fourth time this
year.
In the U.S., investors are betting the Federal Reserve will raise rates in October for the
second time in as many months.
Scott Horsley in Fair News, Washington.
A mob of Israeli settlers stormed into a Palestinian village in the Israeli-occupied West Bank
overnight.
The group attacked a Palestinian family.
After an Israeli court had ordered, they'd be allowed to return home.
NPR's Kat Lonsdorf reports.
More than 100 violent Israeli settlers attacked the village of Jalud, setting fire to buildings
and vehicles and throwing stones, according to the Israeli military.
The attack happened as Israeli security forces were attempting to escort a Palestinian family
back to their home.
That family had been forced to leave their home about two months ago due to continuous
harassment by Israeli settlers, according to an Israeli court order.
Instead, Israeli settlers set fire to the home and the family fled again.
Two of the settlers were arrested and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu condemned
the attack.
Netanyahu recently downplayed such violence in a speech at the U.N.
The U.N. has tracked about 200 settler attacks per month in 2026.
Kat Lonsdorf, NPR News, Tel Aviv.
The U.S. Senate contest in Texas between Republican Ken Paxton and Democrat James Tallarico is
set to shatter campaign advertising records.
From Houston Public Media, Andrew Schneider reports it's unclear how much of a difference
the ad blitz will make.
An analysis from advertising intelligence firm Ad Impact shows that as of mid-September,
Tallarico and groups supporting him had spent more than $53 million across all media, while
Paxton and Pro-Paxton Super PACs spent nearly twice that.
Erica Franklin Fowler of Wesleyan University says advertising matters chiefly at the margins
of a close contest.
It's not going to take a candidate who is not otherwise a good candidate and take them
from somewhere of like 30 percent support over a victory line.
It's really in the, you know, fraction up to a couple percentage points that advertising
can move or benefit a particular candidate.
Most polls either show the two candidates statistically tied or Tallarico with a slim
lead.
I'm Andrew Schneider in Houston.
The South's Joint Chiefs of Staff says their preliminary investigation looked at forensic
evidence, including traces of TNT, the blast crater and the three soldiers' injuries, all
of which were consistent with North Korean land mines.
The Joint Chiefs said that if a final investigation confirms that a North Korean mine caused the
blast, that would constitute an attack on the South and that they would hold Pyongyang
accountable without saying exactly how.
North Korea has been strengthening defenses within the demilitarized zone.
The South suspected they had planted new land mines in the south side of the zone and were
clearing a path to inspect the area when the blast occurred.
Anthony Kuhn in PR News, Seoul.
Director Dennis Haskins has died at the age of 75, according to his agent.
Haskins was best known as the affable but bumbling principal on the hit NBC show, Saved
by the Bell.
As Principal Richard Belding, Haskins oversaw students at the show's Bayside High School.
I'm Corva Coleman, NPR News.

topics.text: Stocks open mixed as oil prices decline slightly due to U.S. war with Iran
Retail gasoline prices drop 2 cents to $4.46 per gallon; airline ticket costs rise
Australia's central bank raises benchmark interest rate for fourth time this year
More than 100 Israeli settlers attack Palestinian village of Jalud in occupied West Bank
U.S. Senate race in Texas between Ken Paxton and James Tallarico shatters ad spending records
South Korea's Joint Chiefs investigate blast that killed three soldiers near North Korean border
Director Dennis Haskins, best known for Saved by the Bell, dies at age 75
